p01.why: The largest array is implementation-defined; the Evidence says Clang rejects this 2^62-byte array and GCC and EDG accept it.

p02.why: A reference to a reference written directly in a declarator is not allowed; collapsing happens only through an alias or template argument.

p04.why: A cv-qualifier applied directly to a reference is not allowed.

p05.why: Top-level const, array parameters and function parameters adjust, so the pairs declare the same functions and every check is true.

p06.why: limit is a const int with a constant initializer, so it is usable as a constant and as an array bound; no main, so not run.

p07.why: Changing a const object during constant evaluation is undefined, and the compilers reject it there.

p08.why: Parentheses around the name have no effect, so p is int*.

p09.why: A local array definition without a bound and without an initializer.

p10.why: (void) and () both declare no parameters, so the types match.

p11.why: Suffixes bind before prefixes and parentheses regroup, giving exactly the stated types.

p12.why: The comma before ... is optional, so f and g have the same type.

p13.why: A reference to void is not allowed.

p14.why: An array of functions is not allowed.

p15.why: A pointer to member of type void is not allowed.

p16.why: const on an array alias goes to the elements, so a is const int[2] and a[0] is a const int lvalue.

p17.why: Writing to a const object with static storage is undefined, and the Evidence says AddressSanitizer stops the write because the storage is read-only.

p18.why: const applied to a reference alias has no effect, so r is int&.

p19.why: Adding const at the inner level of int** needs const at the middle level too.

p20.why: An extern declaration can omit the bound and the definition supplies it.

p21.why: An extern declaration that is not a definition needs no initializer.

p22.why: The two declarations of f disagree on noexcept.

p23.why: Assignment through a pointer to const.

p24.why: The bound is not a constant; the variable-length array extension is rejected under -pedantic-errors.

p25.why: A trailing return type needs auto at the start.

p26.why: Pointers to pointers and to functions are valid, and *pp is an lvalue of type int*.

p27.why: A const scalar definition without an initializer.

p28.why: A function cannot return an array.

p29.why: A named void parameter is not the (void) form.

p31.why: m has a non-constant initializer, so it is not a constant and cannot be an array bound.

p32.why: A class with a constexpr conversion to int is a valid bound type.

p33.why: No implicit conversion adds an array bound.

p34.why: A non-member function cannot have a ref-qualifier.

p35.why: A const floating-point variable cannot occur in a constant expression.

p36.why: The conversion from const int* to int* removes const.

p37.why: Top-level const on a parameter is not part of the type, so both declare one function returning 2.

p38.why: const repeated through an alias counts once, giving const int.

p39.why: constexpr int, an unscoped enumerator, and an integer constant expression are all valid bounds.

p40.why: Qualifiers bind to the type on their left, or on their right when nothing is on the left, giving the stated types.

p41.why: Each conversion adds const and/or drops a bound, and the two-level one has const at the middle level.

p42.why: noexcept is part of the function type, so the types differ.

p44.why: Reference parameters, reference return types and reference members need no initializer.

p45.why: All conversions add qualifiers, and the two-level one has const at the middle level.

p46.why: A static data member declared without a bound gets its bound from the definition.

p47.why: W w(W()) is a function declaration whose parameter is a pointer to a function returning W.

p48.why: Collapsing gives int&& only when both references are rvalue references.

p49.why: An array of references is not allowed.

p50.why: The bound must be greater than zero.

p51.why: A zero bound is rejected under -pedantic-errors.

p52.why: A floating-point type is not a valid bound type.

p53.why: On the 64-bit default target, a 4 GiB array fits in the type of sizeof and the compilers accept it.

p54.why: ... must be the last item of the parameter list.

p55.why: A function type with a cv-qualifier cannot be the target of a pointer.

p56.why: Each declarator applies to its own name, so the types are as stated.

p57.why: w is a function, so w.v is invalid.

p58.why: With -m32 the type of sizeof is 32 bits, so a bound of 2^32 does not fit.

p59.why: A pointer to a reference is not allowed.

p60.why: A reference variable needs an initializer.

p61.why: Three initializers for a bound of two.

p62.why: A const int with a constant initializer is usable in constant expressions.

p63.why: y is not defined const, so writing through the cast is allowed, also at compile time, and f returns 2.

p64.why: A volatile variable cannot occur in a constant expression, so it is not a valid bound.

p65.why: Object pointers convert to void* and const void*.

p66.why: void with another parameter is not the (void) form.

p67.why: The array parameter is an int*, so sizeof gives the pointer size and the function returns 0.

p68.why: A non-member function cannot have a cv-qualifier after its parameter list.

p69.why: A function cannot return a function.

p70.why: const on a function type through an alias has no effect.

p71.why: Dropping a bound at an inner level without const above; GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects (Q-0191).

p72.why: r is another name for x.

p73.why: origin is a const object with static storage, and AddressSanitizer stops the write to read-only storage.

p74.why: The size in bytes, twice the largest sizeof value, does not fit in the type of sizeof.

p75.why: volatile return and parameter types are deprecated, and the warning becomes an error with -Werror -Wdeprecated.

p76.why: An array of void is not allowed.

p77.why: A reference to a ref-qualified function type; EDG 7.0 accepts, Clang and GCC reject (Q-0106).

p78.why: The return type can be const void.

p79.why: The initializer gives the bound; the string literal includes its terminating null.

p80.why: A pointer to a member of reference type is not allowed.

p81.why: Returning pointers to an array and to a function is valid, and the trailing form gives the same type.

p82.why: A const-qualified function alias can declare a member function and be the target of a pointer to member.

p83.why: A scoped enumeration cannot be a bound.

p84.why: The first bound comes from the initializer, and a[0] is an lvalue of int[2].

p86.why: An unbounded array with an empty braced initializer would have zero elements.

p87.why: Array and function parameters become pointers and top-level const is dropped.

p88.why: An extern reference declaration needs no initializer.

p89.why: Only the first bound can be omitted.
